what.text: This page follows asylum seekers from Kyrgyzstan in the United States: people who have asked for international protection and are waiting for a decision.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 6177 Kyrgyz asylum seekers in the United States, 76.5% of all asylum seekers from Kyrgyzstan.
Refugees from Kyrgyzstan, a separate group, live mostly in the United States, France, Germany and the United Kingdom.

why.text: UCDP records an interstate armed conflict between Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan in 2021 and 2022.
The fact pack does not give other reasons why people left Kyrgyzstan.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 2000 at 32 asylum seekers, and the figure was at its highest, 9573, at the end of 2024.
The main years of displacement in the data are 2023 to 2025.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in the United States.
Asylum seekers are counted separately from refugees, as year-end totals for the United States only.
